title: Quick start: from download to your first keys
summary: Download Minimal or Standard, start Lavik from its extracted directory, and connect with redis-cli. No service setup required.

blocks.text: The same startup script works with Minimal and Standard. It uses kernel TCP / io_uring, a disposable 512 MiB file, and the loopback address 127.0.0.1:6379. The two workers each have a 64 MiB registered-buffer budget. Leave this terminal running while you connect from a second terminal.

Press Ctrl-C in the server terminal to stop Lavik. To restart, run the same startup script from the same extracted package directory. The script keeps the existing data file instead of allocating it again. The example uses /tmp/lavik-example for disposable data; /tmp can be cleared by the operating system. Choose persistent storage before storing anything you need to keep.

Extracting an archive does not add its folder to your shell’s PATH. ./lavik explicitly runs the binary in the current directory. A systemd service is optional process management; it does not fix command lookup. Keep using ./lavik here. For an eventual service, use an absolute executable path and a persistent data location rather than this demo directory.

If ./lavik is not found, return to the extracted directory shown in step 1. A GLIBC or shared-library error usually means the OS runtime or Standard dependencies do not match the package requirements. io_uring initialization errors require checking the Linux kernel and sandbox restrictions. If port 6379 is in use, stop your own conflicting demo or choose another port for both the server and redis-cli.

The displayed startup script and client commands are executed against the exact beta package in Linux Docker, starting in the extracted binary directory with no Lavik entry on PATH. The verification also checks a separate value after a graceful shutdown and restart. The package checks cover Minimal and Standard using kernel TCP / io_uring. They do not exercise an SPDK NVMe device, measure performance, or simulate power loss.
